ai.description: This toad reaches 45–50 mm. It is brownish-grey with dark dorsal markings and a pale venter. Key features include a prominent, elongated parotoid gland and a distinct, pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Duttaphrynus mizoramensis* is best distinguished by its distinct, elongated parotoid glands and a unique, continuous row of prominent tubercles along its flanks.
ai.habitat: *Duttaphrynus mizoramensis* inhabits the subtropical evergreen forests of Mizoram, India, typically found near streams at elevations ranging from 700 to 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Kolasib's toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small invertebrates among the leaf litter of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Duttaphrynus mizoramensis* breeds in seasonal streams during the monsoon (June–August), laying eggs in long, gelatinous strings typical of the genus.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Duttaphrynus mizoramensis* is endemic to the state of Mizoram in Northeast India, where it inhabits mid-elevation forest environments.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Duttaphrynus mizoramensis* is a high-pitched, rhythmic series of pulsed notes typically heard near streams in forested habitats.
